content.comment_body: Hello, I'm asking a straightforward question that I couldn't find answered online or from experienced PLC users: Is it possible to establish direct communication between two PLCs using just a fiber optic cable as the physical connection? If so, what extra hardware is required for reliable operation? This setup is needed because both devices are in a remote location, and fiber optic cable is preferred since it will be laid underground with an approximate distance of 3-3.3 km between the units. Thank you in advance.
Hi, Please check this video guide: [url] M.

You'll need a media converter such as the Gigabit Single-Mode Media Converter MC210CS on both ends. This enables you to connect the [product_name] units to the media converters, and then link both converters using a single mode fiber optic cable.

Hi [user_name], The [product_name] devices do not have built-in fiber optic connectors, so you require media converters (as previously mentioned) to convert RJ45 to fiber at each end. For distances up to 3.3 km, multimode fiber cable should work, as it supports lengths up to 5 km. For media converters, there are [company_name] Scalance models: - SCALANCE X101-1 ([article_no]), multimode, up to 5 km - SCALANCE X101-1LD ([article_no]), single mode, up to 26 km Hope this clarifies the setup.

analysis.insight_summary: The user asked how to directly connect two PLCs over long distances using underground fiber optic cable. The main technical challenge is that the selected PLCs lack native fiber optic ports and require additional media converters for connectivity, which makes deployment more involved, particularly for remote installations.
analysis.user_expectations: User seeks a straightforward way to link two PLCs for long-distance, underground communication with fiber optic cabling, preferring minimal extra equipment and clear guidance on required components.
